Despite the safety and wealth gained from his first journey, Sinbad grows restless and sails again. During the second voyage he falls asleep on an island and wakes after his ship has departed. He discovers an enormous roc's egg and ties himself to the adult bird so that it carries him away. The roc deposits him in a deep valley scattered with diamonds but inhabited by giant snakes. Merchants obtain the gems by throwing pieces of meat into the valley so that diamonds stick to them; eagles carry the meat upward, where the merchants drive the birds away. Sinbad fastens himself and a supply of diamonds to one piece, escapes with an eagle, and persuades the startled merchants to help him. He returns to Baghdad richer than before, gives to the poor, and resumes his comfortable life, while continuing his daily hospitality to the porter who hears each voyage.

Sinbad's third expedition is driven into danger and the crew loses its ship before reaching a building inhabited by a huge one-eyed man. The giant imprisons the sailors and kills their captain. Sinbad and the survivors heat iron spits, blind their captor, and flee on rafts, but the giant and his companions destroy most of them with rocks. A great serpent then kills Sinbad's remaining companions before he alone is rescued by a passing ship and eventually returns home. On the fourth voyage, shipwreck leaves Sinbad among cannibals who drug and fatten captives. He avoids their food, escapes, and reaches a kingdom where his knowledge of saddles and bridles earns the ruler's favor. Sinbad marries, then learns that when one spouse dies the survivor is buried alive with the body. After his wife dies, he is sealed in a cavern. He survives on the provisions buried with later victims, finds an animal's route to the coast, and escapes with jewels taken from the cavern. A ship carries him back to Baghdad once more.

On the fifth voyage, Sinbad's fellow merchants break a roc's egg despite his warning. The parent birds retaliate by dropping rocks that destroy the ship. Sinbad reaches an island, where an apparently frail old man asks to be carried across a stream. Once mounted on Sinbad's shoulders, the Old Man of the Sea grips him by the neck and forces him into servitude. Sinbad ferments fruit into wine, makes his captor drunk, and kills him, then escapes with visiting sailors. He profits from gathering coconuts and other trade before returning to Baghdad. His sixth voyage ends in another wreck beside a mountain where earlier victims and rich cargoes have accumulated. With supplies running out, Sinbad builds a raft and follows an underground river through darkness. People on the far side rescue him and bring him to the King of Serendib. The king honors Sinbad and sends him home with gifts and a letter for Caliph Harun al-Rashid. Sinbad delivers them in Baghdad and is rewarded by the caliph.

Harun al-Rashid asks Sinbad to return to Serendib as his envoy. Sinbad delivers the caliph's reply and gifts to the king, but on the homeward journey raiders seize the ship and sell the captives. A merchant who buys Sinbad learns that he is an archer and orders him to hunt elephants for their ivory. Sinbad kills elephants until the herd surrounds him, uproots the tree in which he is hiding, and carries him unharmed to a hidden place filled with elephant bones. He understands that the animals have shown him a source of ivory that makes further hunting unnecessary. His master is delighted by the discovery, grants him freedom, and shares the resulting wealth. Sinbad finally returns to Baghdad and tells the caliph what happened. Having survived his seventh and last voyage, he abandons further travel and lives peacefully on his fortune. The porter finishes hearing the full explanation of Sinbad's wealth and remains his friend and guest.

characters.description: The Dragon Reborn, holding the conquered fortress of Tear and the crystal sword Callandor. Having killed the enemy who tormented his dreams, he has begun to accept his role and to plan boldly, though the dread of the Power's madness and the schemes of the Forsaken close in on every side.
characters.name: Rand al'Thor

characters.description: Rand's luck-blessed friend, freed of the tainted dagger and flush from his gambling, forever trying to slip away from Aes Sedai and prophecy. Reckless and shrewd, he keeps finding that fate drags him back into the Dragon's affairs no matter how he runs.
characters.name: Mat Cauthon

characters.description: Rand's steady friend, a wolfbrother with golden eyes who has grown into a reluctant leader. Deliberate and homesick, he begins to fear for the Two Rivers and the family and neighbors he left behind, and to weigh returning to protect them.
characters.name: Perrin Aybara

characters.description: The innkeeper's daughter of Emond's Field, now an Accepted of the White Tower with a rare talent for entering the world of dreams. Ambitious and determined, she is drawn to study that gift with teachers outside the Tower's rigid halls.
characters.name: Egwene al'Vere

characters.description: The former Wisdom of Emond's Field, a channeler of great strength who can reach the Power only through her own anger. Proud, protective, and relentless, she remains fixed on hunting down the traitor sisters of the Black Ajah.
characters.name: Nynaeve al'Meara

characters.description: The Daughter-Heir of Andor, an Accepted of the Tower and a strong channeler, working with Nynaeve to run down the Black Ajah. Poised and courageous, she is increasingly caught between duty to her throne and her feelings for the Dragon Reborn.
characters.name: Elayne Trakand

characters.description: The Aes Sedai who set the Dragon Reborn on his path, patient and secretive, now finding that Rand will no longer simply do as she counsels. She continues to guide and guard him while pursuing knowledge she shares with no one.
characters.name: Moiraine

characters.description: Moiraine's Warder, a grim and unmatched swordsman and the uncrowned last king of a Borderland realm devoured by the Blight. Bound to Moiraine, he follows her purpose without question wherever it leads.
characters.name: Lan

characters.description: A blunt young woman who reads the future in images only she can see. Having glimpsed her own fate tangled with Rand's, she moves through the intrigues of the Aes Sedai, watching and quietly aiding those she trusts.
characters.name: Min

characters.description: The white-haired gleeman, who survived his earlier stand against a Halfman and travels again with a limp and a carefully hidden past as a onetime royal bard and courtier. Worldly, wry, and shrewd, he lends his knowledge of the wider world to the young people he has come to look after.
characters.name: Thom Merrilin

characters.description: The proud, fierce young woman from a northern land who took the name Faile and devoted herself to Perrin. Courageous and jealous of his attention, she is determined to share whatever dangers he faces rather than be left behind.
characters.name: Faile

characters.description: An Aiel woman of the Waste, a warrior of the Maidens of the Spear, encountered as Rand's road turns toward the Aiel lands. Prickly, proud, and bound by the strict honor code of her people, she regards soft wetlanders with wary disdain and speaks her mind bluntly.
characters.name: Aviendha

recaps.ending: Each of the friends is transformed. In the Aiel Waste, Rand passes through the glass columns of Rhuidean, learns that his people were once oath-bound pacifists in service to the Aes Sedai, and comes out bearing a second Dragon mark and the title of Car'a'carn, He Who Comes With the Dawn. Some clans follow him; others, sickened by the truth he has exposed, will not. He also gains a bound teacher: the Forsaken Asmodean, shielded to a trickle of the Power, is forced to instruct Rand in how to wield saidin and survive it. Mat emerges from an ancient doorway changed, carrying the memories of dead men's wars, a spear, and a medallion that defends against the One Power. In the Two Rivers, Perrin throws back a great Trolloc assault and the interfering Children of the Light, marries Faile, and is acclaimed lord of his homeland. In Tanchico, Elayne and Nynaeve foil the Black Ajah's plot to seize an object that might have leashed Rand, and Nynaeve survives a harrowing clash with the Forsaken Moghedien. And in the White Tower, the Aes Sedai split apart as Elaida seizes the Amyrlin Seat, stills and imprisons Siuan Sanche, and drives loyal sisters into exile. The world is shifting fast around the Dragon Reborn, and old certainties are breaking on every side.
recaps.in_short: Rand leads a small company into the Aiel Waste to claim a prophesied place among its fierce warrior clans. Passing through the ancient glass columns of the city of Rhuidean, he learns the buried truth of the Aiel's origins and emerges marked as the Car'a'carn, the chief of chiefs foretold to unite them and to break them. Mat, drawn through a strange doorway, comes away with old battle memories, a black-hafted spear, and a talisman that turns aside the Power. Perrin, fearing for his home, returns to the Two Rivers with Faile, rallies the villagers against Trolloc raids and Whitecloak meddling stirred up by Padan Fain, wins the fight, marries Faile, and is hailed as their lord. Elayne and Nynaeve track the Black Ajah to the city of Tanchico and thwart their scheme to seize a device that could enslave the Dragon Reborn, while Nynaeve barely survives a duel with the Forsaken Moghedien. Far away, the White Tower tears itself apart as Elaida deposes and stills the Amyrlin Siuan Sanche and seizes power for herself.

recaps.text: Rand al'Thor, a shepherd of the Two Rivers, was carried away with his friends Mat Cauthon and Perrin Aybara by the Aes Sedai Moiraine when Trollocs came hunting them. Through flight, scattering, and the perils of the cursed city of Shadar Logoth, they reached the Eye of the World, where Rand first channeled the One Power and Moiraine named him the Dragon Reborn: the prophesied champion fated to fight the Dark One and, because he wields the tainted male Power, to go mad. In the second book Rand fought the fiery-eyed Ba'alzamon in the sky above Falme before a host of witnesses, was proclaimed the Dragon Reborn for all the world to hear, and first met the Seanchan, ocean-crossing invaders who leash women who can channel. In the third book Rand, fleeing his fate, went to the fortress-city of Tear and drew the crystal sword Callandor from the Stone, an act only the true Dragon could perform, as Aiel warriors stormed the fortress that legend said could never fall. There Moiraine destroyed one waiting Forsaken and Rand killed his fiery-eyed tormentor, learning that the enemy was the Forsaken Ishamael, not the Dark One himself. Meanwhile Mat was freed of his tainted dagger, Perrin bonded ever closer to the wolves and to Faile, and Egwene, Nynaeve, and Elayne trained at the White Tower and struck at the Black Ajah, Aes Sedai secretly sworn to the Shadow. As this book opens Rand holds Tear and Callandor, and must choose how to use the power he has claimed while the Forsaken move against him.

characters.description: A long-serving Shawshank prisoner and the narrator of Andy Dufresne's story. Red is known as the man who can obtain contraband from outside. Practical and observant, he initially regards hope as dangerous in prison, yet his friendship with Andy gradually alters what he believes remains possible.
characters.name: Ellis Redding

characters.description: A quiet former banker sentenced to life at Shawshank for murdering his wife and her lover, crimes he consistently says he did not commit. Andy's financial knowledge makes him useful to guards and administrators, while his patience, self-possession and carefully maintained interests allow him to preserve an inner life the prison cannot fully control.
characters.name: Andy Dufresne

characters.description: The brutal captain of Shawshank's guards. Hadley responds readily to financial advice that saves him money, giving Andy a path to protection and influence, but remains willing to use violence whenever prison authority is challenged.
characters.name: Byron Hadley

characters.description: A later warden of Shawshank who presents himself as devout and disciplined. Norton exploits prison labor and uses Andy's banking skills to conceal corrupt income. Protecting that arrangement matters more to him than evidence that could establish Andy's innocence.
characters.name: Samuel Norton

characters.description: The leader of a group of predatory prisoners known as the Sisters. Bogs repeatedly targets Andy during his early years at Shawshank and represents one of the most immediate dangers of prison life.
characters.name: Bogs Diamond

characters.description: An elderly prisoner who works in Shawshank's library. Brooks has lived inside so long that the institution has become his familiar world. Andy first assists him and then expands the library far beyond what prison officials expected.
characters.name: Brooks Hatlen

characters.description: A younger prisoner whose account of a former cellmate gives Andy the first substantial evidence that someone else committed the murders for which he was convicted. Tommy's information threatens the warden's control over Andy.
characters.name: Tommy Williams

characters.description: A violent criminal whom Tommy Williams once heard boasting that he murdered a golfer and the golfer's lover while her banker husband was imprisoned for it. The story closely matches the crime attributed to Andy.
characters.name: Elmo Blatch

recaps.ending: Andy escapes through a tunnel he excavated behind successive pinup posters, then crawls through a prison sewer and disappears. Using the false identity under which he had helped Warden Norton hide corrupt income, he withdraws the accumulated money and sends records of the scheme to the press. The resulting scandal ends Norton's career and exposes Shawshank's abuses. Red later receives a blank postcard from a Texas border town, confirming that Andy is free. After Red is paroled, he struggles with the disorientation that comes from spending most of his adult life in prison. He follows Andy's old directions to a Maine field and finds money and a letter inviting him to join Andy in Zihuatanejo, Mexico. Red breaks parole and travels south. The narrative ends before their reunion, with Red choosing uncertainty and hope over the safe routines of confinement.
recaps.in_short: At Shawshank prison, contraband supplier Red befriends Andy Dufresne, a banker serving life for two murders he says he did not commit. Andy survives assault, builds a respected prison library and becomes indispensable to guards who need financial help. Warden Samuel Norton forces him to conceal corrupt income. When prisoner Tommy Williams brings evidence identifying another killer, Norton suppresses it to keep Andy under his control. For years Andy has also asked Red for small items, including a rock hammer and posters. He uses the hammer to dig through his cell wall, hides the tunnel behind the posters and escapes through a sewer. He takes Norton's hidden money under a false identity and exposes the corruption. After parole, Red finds cash and an invitation Andy left for him in Maine. He violates parole and heads toward Mexico, sustained by the hope of seeing his friend again.

recaps.text: Ellis Redding, known as Red, is serving a long sentence at Shawshank and has built a reputation for obtaining forbidden goods. He becomes interested in Andy Dufresne, a former banker convicted of murdering his wife and her lover. Andy insists he is innocent and carries himself with unusual reserve. He asks Red for a small rock hammer and later for pinup posters. During his early years he is repeatedly assaulted by Bogs Diamond and the Sisters, but his banking knowledge eventually gives him protection: he advises guard captain Byron Hadley and begins handling financial matters for prison staff. Andy also works in the library, secures funds and books, and turns it into a valuable institution. Under Warden Samuel Norton, his skills acquire a darker purpose. Norton profits from prison labor and compels Andy to maintain the hidden accounts behind a fictitious identity. A younger inmate, Tommy Williams, later reports that a former cellmate named Elmo Blatch confessed to the murders attributed to Andy. Norton refuses to pursue evidence that could free the man managing his money and uses punishment and transfer to silence the matter. Andy appears to accept that legal rescue is closed, but eventually vanishes from a locked cell. He has spent years cutting a tunnel through the wall with the rock hammer and concealing it behind his posters. After crawling through a sewer to freedom, he assumes control of Norton's secret funds and sends evidence of the corruption to a newspaper, destroying the warden's position. Red receives a postcard suggesting Andy reached the border. When Red is finally paroled, freedom feels alien after decades of institutional life. He follows directions Andy once gave him, finds money and a letter hidden in a Maine field, and chooses to break parole and travel to Zihuatanejo. The story closes with Red moving toward the friend who taught him that hope can be worth the risk.

characters.description: A small piglet won by Farmer Hogget at a village fair. Separated from his mother, Babe is taken into the farmyard and adopted by the sheepdog Fly. He is curious, courteous, and willing to learn, and gradually wonders why a pig should not do the work of a dog.
characters.name: Babe

characters.description: A quiet, observant farmer who wins Babe by correctly estimating the piglet's weight. Hogget pays close attention to the animals and is prepared to test an unlikely idea when he notices Babe's unusual understanding of sheep.
characters.name: Farmer Hogget

characters.description: Farmer Hogget's practical and talkative wife. She views Babe first as a useful prize for the farm and is much less inclined than her husband to imagine that the piglet might have an extraordinary future.
characters.name: Mrs Hogget

characters.description: Hogget's experienced border collie, who takes charge of the newly arrived piglet and allows him to call her mother. Fly teaches Babe about farm life and sheepdog work, combining affection with the habits and assumptions of a working dog.
characters.name: Fly

characters.description: Fly's mate and another of Hogget's working sheepdogs. Proud of the traditional skills of his kind, Rex is doubtful that a pig belongs in the work for which sheepdogs have been bred and trained.
characters.name: Rex

characters.description: The oldest and most respected ewe in Hogget's flock. Maa responds to Babe's good manners and helps him understand that sheep cooperate when they are addressed with courtesy rather than insults and threats.
characters.name: Maa

characters.description: The flock on Hogget's farm, wary of dogs but willing to judge Babe by his behavior. Their trust gives him a way of moving sheep based on requests and cooperation rather than fear.
characters.name: Hogget's Sheep

recaps.ending: At the Grand Challenge Sheepdog Trials, the unfamiliar sheep initially refuse to obey Babe. Help from Fly and the farm flock allows him to establish that he approaches sheep as a trusted equal rather than a predator. Once Babe addresses the trial flock in the manner sheep recognize, they cooperate. He guides them through the required course calmly and accurately, astonishing the judges and spectators. Babe and Farmer Hogget receive a perfect score and win the competition. The result proves Hogget's faith in the piglet and vindicates Babe's belief that respect can accomplish what intimidation cannot. Farmer and pig share a quiet acknowledgment of work well done, with Babe now accepted as a true sheep-pig.
recaps.in_short: Farmer Hogget wins a piglet at a fair and brings him home, where the border collie Fly adopts him and names him Babe. Fascinated by sheepdog work, Babe tries herding and discovers that sheep respond far better to his courtesy than to a dog's threats. The old ewe Maa helps him earn the flock's trust, while Hogget notices the piglet's ability and begins training him. Hogget eventually enters Babe in the Grand Challenge Sheepdog Trials despite widespread disbelief that a pig can compete. At the event, unfamiliar sheep initially ignore Babe. With help from Fly and the sheep at home, Babe gains their confidence and politely guides them through the course. He earns a perfect score, wins the trial for Hogget, and is recognized as a genuine sheep-pig.

recaps.text: At a village fair, Farmer Hogget correctly guesses the weight of a piglet and wins him as a prize. The bewildered young pig is taken to Hogget's farm, where the border collie Fly comforts him and takes on a mother's role. She calls him Babe and begins teaching him how the farm works. Babe watches Fly control the sheep and becomes fascinated by her job. The dogs assume sheep must be driven by commands and threats, but Babe is naturally polite and questions why the animals are treated as foolish. When he meets Maa, the flock's senior ewe, she responds to his courtesy and begins to explain the sheep's point of view. Babe starts to see that cooperation may work better than fear.

Babe asks to learn sheepdog work. His size and species make the idea seem absurd, and the working dogs are not all pleased by it, but Fly teaches him the basic tasks. Babe does not imitate the dogs' hostile language. He asks the sheep to move, listens to their concerns, and relies on the trust Maa has helped him establish. The flock consequently does what he requests with less resistance than it shows the dogs. Farmer Hogget quietly observes Babe's results. Rather than dismissing what he sees, he begins working with the piglet and testing whether Babe can respond to signals and guide sheep with the precision expected from a trained dog.

Hogget's private experiment becomes an ambitious plan: he enters Babe in the Grand Challenge Sheepdog Trials. Mrs Hogget and others expect embarrassment, while experienced handlers have no reason to take a pig seriously. Babe continues training with Fly and the farm flock, learning the sequence of movements he will need to perform. His method still depends on sheep choosing to cooperate, so success with animals who know him does not guarantee that an unfamiliar flock will listen. Hogget nevertheless brings Babe to the competition and presents him for inspection. The rules do not provide a simple reason to exclude him, and the unlikely pair are allowed to attempt the course.

At the trial, Babe enters the field to astonishment and laughter. The unfamiliar sheep distrust him and initially refuse to move, placing the whole attempt in danger. Fly and the sheep back at Hogget's farm help bridge the gap, enabling Babe to approach the trial flock with the form of greeting and respect sheep extend to one another. Once they understand that he will not bully them, the sheep agree to cooperate. Babe guides them through the gates and pen with calm accuracy. The judges award him a perfect score, and he and Farmer Hogget win the trial. Babe's success establishes him not as a pig copying a dog, but as a sheep-pig whose courtesy is the source of his skill.

characters.description: An American composer traveling through North Africa after the Second World War with his wife, Kit. He insists on distinguishing himself from a tourist because he expects to remain abroad indefinitely. Introspective and emotionally remote, he hopes that moving farther from familiar life may repair a marriage that has grown strained.
characters.name: Port Moresby

characters.description: Port's wife and traveling companion. Intelligent, anxious, and strongly influenced by omens, she tries to control uncertainty through private rituals and predictions. Her marriage to Port is marked by affection, distance, and an inability to speak plainly about what either of them wants.
characters.name: Kit Moresby

characters.description: A prosperous young American traveling with Port and Kit for part of their journey. Sociable, confident, and more conventionally touristic than Port, he is attracted to Kit. His presence gives the couple companionship but also intensifies their jealousy and marital tension.
characters.name: Tunner

characters.description: A local man who attaches himself to Port during a solitary night walk through the coastal city. Acting as guide and intermediary, he leads Port away from the European quarter and arranges a meeting with Marhnia.
characters.name: Smaïl

characters.description: A young woman whom Port meets beyond the city through Smaïl. Her encounter with him combines intimacy, bargaining, and danger, immediately unsettling Port's wish to experience the region outside the protections of ordinary tourism.
characters.name: Marhnia

characters.description: An English travel writer moving through North Africa with her adult son, Eric. Loud, domineering, and dismissive of most people she meets, she presents herself as an authority on the region while depending on the same colonial travel network as the other foreigners.
characters.name: Mrs. Lyle

characters.description: Mrs. Lyle's adult son and traveling companion. Talkative and ingratiating, he complains about his dependence on his mother while continuing to live within it. His shifting stories and requests make him an uncomfortable presence among Port, Kit, and Tunner.
characters.name: Eric Lyle

characters.description: A merchant whom Kit encounters after she has fled alone into the desert. He takes her into a caravan, gives her male clothing for the journey, and forms an intense relationship with her as they travel toward his home.
characters.name: Belqassim

recaps.ending: After Port dies of typhoid at a remote French outpost, Kit abandons the protections of the foreign community and moves alone into the Sahara. She joins a caravan and becomes attached to the merchant Belqassim, traveling disguised as a boy and then living concealed in his household. The relationship that initially gives form to her flight becomes another kind of confinement. When her presence is discovered and the household turns against her, she escapes into the city. Representatives of the American consulate locate her and try to return her to the world she left, where Tunner is waiting. Kit flees from them before the reunion can occur. The novel closes without restoring her to her former identity or relationships: she disappears into the streets, psychologically dislocated and alone, while Tunner remains separated from her.
recaps.in_short: Port and Kit Moresby, an estranged American couple, travel through postwar North Africa with their affluent acquaintance Tunner. Port treats endless travel as an alternative to ordinary life, while Kit's anxiety and superstition sharpen as the party moves inland. Their companion's attraction to Kit, her sexual encounter with him, Port's solitary pursuits, and the theft of Port's passport deepen the couple's isolation. Port and Kit eventually leave Tunner behind and continue toward the Sahara, where Port contracts typhoid. Kit nurses him at a remote outpost, but he dies. She then flees alone into the desert, joins a caravan, and enters an intense relationship with the merchant Belqassim, who hides her in his household. After being discovered and driven out, she is found by consular officials but escapes before they can reunite her with Tunner. Kit vanishes into the city, severed from the life and identity with which she began the journey.

recaps.text: After the Second World War, Americans Port and Kit Moresby arrive in a North African port with their friend Tunner. Port calls himself a traveler rather than a tourist and imagines continuing indefinitely into unfamiliar territory. His marriage to Kit is already strained: they remain attached to one another but move through separate emotional worlds, while Tunner's open sociability and interest in Kit complicate the balance. Port wanders alone at night beyond the European quarter. Guided by Smaïl, he meets Marhnia, an encounter that turns threatening and leaves his romantic idea of entering an unknown culture unsettled. Kit, meanwhile, responds to uncertainty through private omens and fearful predictions.

The travelers encounter Mrs. Lyle, an overbearing English travel writer, and her dependent adult son Eric. Their company creates new frictions as the group prepares to move inland. Port remains wary of Tunner's ease with Kit, while Kit resents Port's emotional distance and the freedom he claims for himself. The Lyles embody another version of foreign travel: Mrs. Lyle speaks as an authority while treating the region and its people chiefly as material for her own purposes. Eric tries to ingratiate himself with the Americans but inspires little trust. Rather than drawing Port and Kit together, movement away from the coast gives each of them more opportunities to avoid the conflict within their marriage.

As the party travels farther inland, Port and Kit repeatedly separate and reunite without resolving their estrangement. Kit travels with Tunner and sleeps with him, an act shaped by attraction, resentment, and her fear that Port has already withdrawn from her. Port's passport disappears, leaving him dependent on distant officials and uncertain whether the loss was accidental. The practical difficulty mirrors his growing sense that the identity and protections he carried from home are becoming less secure. The Lyles' behavior adds suspicion and disorder, while Port becomes increasingly determined to put distance between the couple and Tunner.

Port and Kit continue south without Tunner, seeking a place beyond the routes and relationships that have constrained them. Their isolation briefly forces a renewed closeness, but Port falls seriously ill. In the remote settlements near the desert there is little medical support, and travel becomes difficult. Kit tries to care for him and find help while confronting the possibility she has long displaced into omens. Port's fever and weakness increase, leaving the couple dependent on sparse colonial administration and on people with whom they share little language or understanding. The journey that Port imagined as an escape from fixed life has become physical entrapment.

Port is suffering from typhoid and deteriorates at an isolated French outpost. Kit nurses him with limited assistance, but neither effort nor renewed intimacy can reverse the illness. As he dies, the familiar world represented by their marriage and shared travel collapses for her. Kit does not wait to be taken back into the network of officials and foreign travelers. Overwhelmed and psychologically unmoored, she leaves Port's body and moves alone into the desert. Her departure is not a planned continuation of their journey but a flight from the identity, obligations, and grief attached to his death.

Alone beyond the foreign travel routes, Kit attaches herself to a caravan. The merchant Belqassim disguises her in male clothing, enabling her to travel with the men, and the two begin an intense sexual relationship. The desert movement and the disguise allow Kit to abandon her former social identity, at least temporarily. Belqassim eventually takes her to his home and conceals her in a private room. What began as release from the world associated with Port becomes dependence on Belqassim and separation from everyone around her. Unable to communicate freely or control where she goes, Kit occupies a hidden, precarious place in his household.

Belqassim's household discovers Kit's presence, ending the secrecy that protected her and exposing the hostility around her position. She escapes and wanders into the city, vulnerable and detached from ordinary measures of safety. Officials eventually identify her and place her in the care of the American consulate. Tunner, who has been trying to find her, waits to receive her and imagines a return to their earlier world. Before that reunion, Kit runs away from the consular escort. She disappears into the streets rather than resume her place as Port's widow or Tunner's companion. The journey ends with Port dead and Kit alive but profoundly dislocated, beyond the relationships and social identity with which she entered North Africa.

characters.description: The witch of the Chalk, now in her late teens and fully established in her own country: land of her own, a cottage, a reputation, and more work than one person can reasonably do. She nurses, delivers, buries, arbitrates, and flies out at any hour, and she has learned to treat exhaustion as part of the job. The world around her is changing quickly, with railways, machinery, and iron spreading across the Disc, and she is more aware than most that old things do not simply go away because the times have moved on.
characters.name: Tiffany Aching

characters.description: The senior witch of the Ramtops, austere, undemonstrative, and acknowledged without any formal title as the one the other witches measure themselves against. She lives alone in a small cottage in Lancre with her bees and her white cat, keeps her steading in perfect order, and has spent a lifetime standing between her country and the things that would come into it if nobody was watching. She has a very clear sense of when things need doing.
characters.name: Granny Weatherwax

characters.description: The other great witch of Lancre: warm, disreputable, endlessly sociable, and the matriarch of a very large family. Where Granny Weatherwax is respected, Nanny Ogg is liked, which she has always known is the more useful of the two. She has been in on every serious piece of witching in the mountains for decades.
characters.name: Nanny Ogg

characters.description: The Big Man of the Nac Mac Feegle of the Chalk, the small blue fighting men who consider Tiffany their hag and follow her everywhere whether or not this is convenient. Loud, entirely fearless, and married to a kelda who takes a firm line on unnecessary fighting.
characters.name: Rob Anybody

characters.description: The kelda of the Chalk's Feegle mound, small and sharp, who governs the clan and can see some way into what is coming. She has begun to feel something moving in the old places that ought to be shut.
characters.name: Jeannie

characters.description: Rob Anybody's brother, cheerfully enthusiastic and reliably a step or two behind the conversation.
characters.name: Daft Wullie

characters.description: A small white cat belonging to Granny Weatherwax, self-possessed, unimpressed, and quite capable of walking into places that other creatures avoid.
characters.name: You

characters.description: The Baron of the Chalk, Tiffany's childhood friend, now married and running the estate, and rather better at the job than either of them expected.
characters.name: Roland

characters.description: The Baroness of the Chalk, married to Roland, and a trained witch in her own right who quietly keeps a library and does useful work without making a performance of it. She and Tiffany, once rivals, get on rather well.
characters.name: Letitia

characters.description: Tiffany's young man, away in Ankh-Morpork training as a doctor at the free hospital. Bookish, precise about words, and unfailingly kind, he writes when he can and visits when the work lets him, which is not often.
characters.name: Preston

characters.description: The Queen of the elves, beautiful, glamorous, and utterly without pity, who rules her court by fear and regards humans as entertainment and as material. She has been kept out of the human world for many years and has not forgiven it.
characters.name: Nightshade

characters.description: The third son of a rich, bullying lord, who has run away from a future he wants nothing to do with and turned up in Lancre announcing that he intends to be a witch. Gentle, stubborn, and unusually good at calming animals and people and at getting the quarrelling parties in a room to stop shouting, he is entirely unbothered by being told that men do not do this.
characters.name: Geoffrey Swivel

characters.description: Geoffrey's goat: an animal of considerable presence, disturbing intelligence, and firm opinions, who accompanies him everywhere and is not to be argued with.
characters.name: Mephistopheles

characters.description: An ambitious elf lord of the Queen's court, cruel even by elvish standards and impatient with a ruler he considers to have gone soft. He believes the human world has become weak and distracted and is ripe for taking back.
characters.name: Lord Peaseblossom

characters.description: The Queen of Lancre, once a witch herself and still one underneath the crown and the royal duties. Vague-seeming, soft-hearted, and considerably harder than she looks when something threatens her kingdom or her children.
characters.name: Magrat Garlick

characters.description: A self-important witch much occupied with the correct occult vocabulary, jewellery, and ceremony, and with her own standing among the other witches. She is quick to explain what proper witchcraft consists of and slow to do any of the unpleasant parts of it.
characters.name: Mrs Earwig

recaps.ending: The elves invade the Chalk in force, and Tiffany meets them with everything she can gather: the witches, the Nac Mac Feegle, the goblins with their ironwork, the villagers and shepherds, Geoffrey's shed full of old men, Magrat in armour again, and the land itself, which knows her. Nightshade, who has learned in exile what it is to be on the receiving end of cruelty, turns against her own kind and is killed for it by Peaseblossom. Tiffany faces Peaseblossom herself and destroys him, and the elves are broken and driven back through the mound, with the way closed behind them and iron and machinery making the human world a place they can no longer easily enter. Afterwards the arrangements settle: Geoffrey takes over Granny Weatherwax's cottage and steading in Lancre and proves to be exactly the right person for it, so Tiffany is no longer trying to be the witch of two countries at once and can be wholly the witch of the Chalk. Nanny Ogg is left as the senior witch of the mountains, in her own quite different way. Preston comes home when he can, and Tiffany's future with him is understood without being settled. At the last, Tiffany takes the shepherd's crown, the small fossil out of the chalk that she has carried since the beginning, and puts it back into the ground on the downs where it belongs.
recaps.in_short: Granny Weatherwax, the senior witch of the Ramtops, sets her house in order, dies at a time of her own choosing, and leaves her cottage and her steading to Tiffany Aching. Tiffany, already stretched thin as the witch of the Chalk, tries to hold both countries at once and wears herself out doing it, while the witches argue about who should really have inherited. With Granny gone, the barrier that kept the elves out of the human world is weak, and Lord Peaseblossom deposes the elf Queen Nightshade and prepares an invasion. Nightshade, thrown out into a world full of iron, is taken in by the witches and slowly learns what it is like to be the one who is helpless. Meanwhile Geoffrey Swivel, a runaway young man who wants to be a witch, arrives in Lancre and turns out to have a real gift for calming trouble. The elves raid, then attack the Chalk outright. Tiffany gathers witches, Feegles, goblins, villagers, and the land itself, Nightshade dies turning against her own kind, and Tiffany destroys Peaseblossom and closes the way. Geoffrey takes Granny's steading, and Tiffany becomes wholly and only the Chalk's witch.

recaps.text: Previously, in earlier books: Tiffany Aching, granddaughter of a much-loved Chalk shepherd, discovered a witch's talent as a child and went into the Queen of the Fairies' country of dreams to bring her stolen brother home, helped by the Nac Mac Feegle, the tiny blue fighting men who call her their hag. Trained in the mountains, she survived possession by an ancient mindless hiver, and later stepped into an old midwinter dance and had to end the elemental spirit of winter, and the endless winter he caused, herself. At sixteen she was hunted across her own country by the Cunning Man, the eyeless remnant of a long-dead witch-hunter who turned the Chalk against her, and destroyed him by running through fire as a hare. She has been the Chalk's acknowledged witch ever since, with land and a cottage of her own. Roland, her childhood friend, is now the Baron and married to Letitia; her young man Preston is away in Ankh-Morpork training as a doctor; and the world beyond the Chalk is filling up with railways, machinery, and iron. In Lancre, Granny Weatherwax remains the witch the other witches defer to.

Tiffany's days on the Chalk are the ordinary, endless business of a working witch: sick rooms, births, deaths, feuds, old people nobody else will visit, and a great deal of flying between one emergency and the next on no sleep. The Chalk itself is changing, with the wider world's new machinery and iron reaching even the downs, and with goblins, now recognized as people, taking cheerfully to metalwork and machines. In Lancre, Granny Weatherwax is going about her own rounds and putting her cottage and her steading into a state of unusual order, tidying, mending, settling accounts, and making arrangements with a deliberateness that the bees and the cat notice before anyone else does. Elsewhere, in a place that is not quite anywhere, something old and beautiful and cruel has begun to test the walls of the world, and to notice that the watch on them is not what it was.

Granny Weatherwax dies. She has arranged everything down to the last detail, including who is to be told and in what order, and she leaves her cottage and her whole Lancre steading to Tiffany Aching. The witches gather from across the mountains for a funeral that is also, unmistakably, the end of an era, and the question of who is now the senior witch is left conspicuously unanswered, with Nanny Ogg refusing the role and Mrs Earwig very willing to discuss her own claim. Tiffany, who did not ask for any of it, tries to do both jobs at once, flying between Lancre and the Chalk day after day and steadily wearing herself out, and finds that the people of Lancre are not sure they want a girl from the lowlands as their witch. And with Granny gone, the thing she had been quietly standing in the way of for years discovers that the way is open.

In the elves' country, Lord Peaseblossom moves against the Queen. Nightshade has ruled by glamour and terror for centuries, but the human world has been filling up with iron, engines, and people who no longer believe in her, and her court decides that she has grown weak. She is deposed and thrown out into a world that burns her, and the witches, who have every reason to leave her where she fell, take her in instead. Meanwhile Geoffrey Swivel arrives in Lancre: the unwanted third son of a bullying lord, run away from home, entirely serious about becoming a witch, and accompanied by a goat with opinions. Nanny Ogg takes him on. He has no obvious magic, but he can calm an argument, an animal, or a frightened person simply by being present, which turns out to be a rarer talent than anyone expects.

Nightshade, kept alive and being taught the humiliating human skills of being helpless, gradually comes to understand what her own kind have always done to people, which is not a lesson elves are built for. Geoffrey settles into Lancre and quietly changes it, gathering the old men who have been left with nothing to do into a shed of their own where they can work, argue, and be useful again. Tiffany is stretched past what one witch can manage, resented in Lancre for holding Granny's cottage and missed on the Chalk when she is away, and the other witches are divided over her. And the raids begin: elves slipping through into the human world in ones and twos, stealing, tormenting, killing livestock, and testing what the people of the Chalk and the mountains will do about it. Peaseblossom is measuring the ground for something much larger.

The raids turn into a campaign. The elves work through the old mound on the Chalk, and this time they do not go away when they are chased off; people are hurt, a child is taken, and the countryside learns what it had forgotten about what elves actually are. Tiffany calls in everyone she can: the Nac Mac Feegle, who have been waiting their whole lives for exactly this; the witches of the mountains, including the ones who have been arguing about her; the goblins, whose ironwork is a weapon in itself; and the shepherds, blacksmiths, and villagers of the Chalk. Nightshade, now something no elf has been before, tells them what her people fear and how their glamour works, and has to decide whether she is with the world that took her in or with the court that threw her out. Magrat Garlick, Queen of Lancre, takes her witchcraft and her iron back out of storage.

Peaseblossom brings his whole court through onto the Chalk, and the fighting is real, frightening, and costly. The elves' glamour turns people against each other and makes them see what is not there, and it has to be broken person by person; iron, cold and everywhere in the new world of tools and machines and rails, hurts the elves more than they had allowed for. Nightshade turns openly against her own kind and fights alongside the witches, and Peaseblossom kills her for it. The Feegles fight the way they have always wanted to. Geoffrey does what nobody else can and calms the terror the elves live on. Tiffany, standing on the ground she has known all her life and which knows her, works her way toward Peaseblossom himself, because this is not something she can hand to anyone else.

Tiffany faces Peaseblossom and destroys him, and with their leader gone the elves are broken and driven back through the mound, which is shut behind them; between the iron and the machinery of the new world and what has just happened to them, the elves will not be coming back easily. Nightshade is dead, having ended as something no elf had been before. Afterwards the arrangements settle themselves: Geoffrey takes on Granny Weatherwax's cottage and steading, which he is plainly right for, so Tiffany is released from trying to be the witch of two countries and can be entirely the witch of the Chalk; Nanny Ogg is left as the senior witch of the mountains, in her own quite different fashion. Preston comes home when the hospital lets him, and what is between them is understood rather than announced. At the last, Tiffany takes the shepherd's crown, the small fossil out of the chalk she has carried since the start, and puts it back into the ground on the downs where it belongs.

characters.description: A recovering alcoholic and former prep-school English teacher who takes the job of winter caretaker at the isolated Overlook Hotel, hoping the quiet months will let him finish his writing and rebuild his life. He is a talented, ambitious man with a violent temper he can no longer excuse: he lost his teaching post after beating a student who vandalized his car, and once, drunk, he broke his small son's arm. He has stayed sober for months through sheer will, helped by his friend Al Shockley, but resentment and self-doubt gnaw at him. He loves his wife and son and is terrified of failing them, yet part of him chafes at the burden of family. The caretaker post is his last chance to prove he can hold everything together.
characters.name: Jack Torrance

characters.description: Jack's wife and Danny's mother, a watchful, self-reliant woman whose marriage has been strained near to breaking by Jack's drinking and temper. She grew up under a cruel, domineering mother and is determined that her own child will be safe and loved. She stayed with Jack after he broke Danny's arm, and she watches her husband constantly for signs of relapse, torn between hope that the fresh start at the Overlook will save them and fear of being trapped, snowbound, with a man she is no longer sure she can trust.
characters.name: Wendy Torrance

characters.description: The Torrances' five-year-old son, an unusually perceptive and gentle boy who possesses a powerful psychic gift. He can sometimes sense the thoughts and moods of the people around him and glimpse things that have happened or are about to happen. His visions reach him through Tony, a figure only he can see, who shows him frightening images he does not understand, including a word that appears in mirror writing. Bright and articulate beyond his years, Danny feels the tension between his parents keenly and tries to shield them from his fear, terrified that the family will come apart.
characters.name: Danny Torrance

characters.description: A figure that appears only to Danny, whom the boy thinks of as a kind of imaginary friend. Tony shows Danny visions of things distant in place or time, some reassuring and many alarming, and speaks to him in warnings the boy cannot always interpret. Tony began appearing during episodes of Danny's psychic gift and becomes his guide to the dangers gathering around the family, though Danny does not fully understand who or what Tony is.
characters.name: Tony

characters.description: The Overlook Hotel's officious manager, a small, self-important man who interviews Jack for the caretaker position and makes clear that he opposed the hiring. He takes obvious pride in the resort's prestigious guest list and is defensive about its darker past, which he recounts only reluctantly, including the previous caretaker who killed his family during a winter alone at the hotel. Cold and disapproving, he treats Jack with barely concealed distaste.
characters.name: Stuart Ullman

characters.description: A previous winter caretaker of the Overlook, whose story Jack is told when he is hired. Some years earlier Grady, isolated and unbalanced by the long snowbound months, killed his wife and two young daughters and then himself inside the hotel. His name and his crime hang over the Torrances' stay from the beginning, an example of what the empty place and its solitude can do to the man left alone to mind it.
characters.name: Grady

characters.description: The Overlook Hotel's head cook, a warm, plain-spoken man from Florida who works the resort each summer and helps close it down for the winter. He shares Danny's psychic gift, which he calls 'the shining,' and recognizes at once that the boy has it more strongly than anyone he has met. Before he leaves for the season he quietly warns Danny that an old, empty hotel can hold echoes of terrible things, cautions him to stay out of certain rooms, and tells him that if he is ever in real danger he can call out with his mind, and Hallorann will hear him and come.
characters.name: Dick Hallorann

characters.description: A grand, isolated resort hotel high in the Colorado mountains, cut off from the world by snow through the long winter. Gracious and storied on the surface, it has a violent history stretching back decades: suicides, gangland killings, and the caretaker who murdered his family within its walls. The hotel seems to retain and feed on the dreadful things that have happened inside it, and it exerts a growing, malevolent pull on the family left alone to mind it, drawn most of all to the psychic gift of the youngest of them.
characters.name: The Overlook Hotel

recaps.ending: The Overlook's hold on Jack becomes total, and the thing wearing his shape hunts Wendy and Danny with a roque mallet, badly injuring Wendy. Danny, summoned to face his father, refuses to run and instead reminds the possessed man of the hotel's oldest chore: the boiler in the basement, whose pressure must be dumped daily or it will blow. Jack had forgotten it. For a moment the real Jack surfaces, tells his son he loves him, and sends him away before the hotel reclaims him and he rushes to the boiler too late. The pressure has climbed past saving, and the Overlook is torn apart in the explosion; Jack and the malevolent presence die together in the fire. Hallorann, who has driven and struggled through the blizzard from Florida, gets Wendy and Danny out on a snowmobile as the hotel burns. In a closing summer scene, the three are together at a Maine resort where Hallorann has taken work; Wendy is healing, and the cook comforts Danny, telling the grieving boy that he must go on living and feeling, and that his father's love for him was real even though the place destroyed him.
recaps.in_short: Jack Torrance, a recovering alcoholic writer with a history of violence, takes a job as winter caretaker of the remote Overlook Hotel in the Colorado mountains, bringing his wife Wendy and their five-year-old son Danny. Danny has a psychic gift, the shining, and the hotel's cook Hallorann, who shares it, warns the boy that the place holds dangerous echoes of its bloody past. Once the snow seals them in, the Overlook begins to work on the family, feeding on Danny's power and on Jack's weaknesses. Jack unravels, drawn deeper into the hotel's influence and its history, and finally, possessed, he attacks his wife and son with a mallet. Danny calls out to Hallorann, who fights back through a blizzard to reach them. In the end Danny stops his father by reminding the hotel's servant of the old boiler that Jack has forgotten to tend; the pressure builds until it explodes, destroying the Overlook. Jack dies with it, but Wendy, Danny, and Hallorann escape.

recaps.text: Jack Torrance interviews with the manager Stuart Ullman and is hired as the winter caretaker of the Overlook Hotel, an elegant, remote resort in the Colorado Rockies that closes for the snowbound months. Jack is a recovering alcoholic and a would-be writer, recently fired from teaching for beating a student, and haunted by the night he drunkenly broke the arm of his young son. He hopes the isolation will help him finish his work and mend himself. His wife Wendy is wary, watching for any sign that he will drink again, and their five-year-old son Danny is no ordinary child: he has a psychic gift and is visited by a figure called Tony, who shows him disturbing visions, among them the hotel and a word he sees spelled backward. Jack is warned of the Overlook's grim history, including a former caretaker who murdered his family there, but he needs the job too badly to refuse it.

The Torrances arrive at the Overlook on closing day and tour the sprawling, empty hotel. Danny meets the head cook, Dick Hallorann, who shares the boy's gift and calls it 'the shining.' Hallorann gently warns Danny that a place as old as the Overlook can hold lingering traces of the terrible things that happened in it, tells him to keep away from certain rooms, and promises that if Danny is ever in real trouble he can call out to him with his mind across any distance. The staff and the last guests depart, the great hotel falls silent, and with the first heavy snows the family is left alone and increasingly cut off from the outside world, settling into their winter routine as Jack begins his caretaking duties and his writing.

As the family settles in, the Overlook begins to reveal itself. Danny senses menace throughout the hotel and is troubled by the recurring vision of the mirror-writing word. Jack, exploring the building, discovers a scrapbook full of the resort's violent and scandalous history and grows obsessed with it, feeling the place take hold of his imagination. Ordinary features of the hotel start to seem wrong: the ornamental hedge animals in the garden appear to shift and move when no one is looking, and the pressure of isolation begins to tell on all three of them. Wendy watches Jack's moods darken, and Danny, frightened by what he feels but unwilling to add to his parents' burdens, keeps much of his fear to himself even as the hotel's influence steadily deepens.

The hotel's power turns openly hostile. Drawn by curiosity and by the pull of the place, Danny enters the forbidden Room 217 and is attacked by the corpse-like figure of a dead woman in the bathtub, escaping badly shaken and marked. When his parents find bruises on him, suspicion and fear ripple through the family. Jack, meanwhile, slides further under the Overlook's spell, his resentments sharpening and his grip on himself loosening even though he has not had a drink. Cut off by deepening snow, the Torrances can no longer simply leave, and Danny understands with growing dread that the hotel wants him and is using his father to get at him.

Jack falls fully into the hotel's orbit. In the deserted ballroom he encounters a phantom bartender who serves him drinks that should not exist, and the Overlook feeds his craving and his rage, promising him importance and belonging if he will give it his son. The ghosts of the hotel's past grow bolder, and Jack begins taking their side against his own family. To make sure no one can call for help or flee, he sabotages the family's link to the outside world, wrecking the radio and disabling the snowmobile. Wendy realizes that her husband has become a danger to them and that they are trapped with him, while Danny, cornered by the thing the hotel is making of his father, reaches out with his mind toward the only person who might save them.

Danny's desperate psychic cry reaches Hallorann in Florida, and the cook drops everything to fight his way back to Colorado through a brutal blizzard, struggling toward the hotel against the storm and the Overlook's efforts to stop him. At the hotel, Jack is all but gone, possessed by the place and armed with a heavy roque mallet, and he hunts Wendy through the corridors, injuring her savagely before she manages to hold him off. Danny, drawn out to confront his father, sees that the man before him is now mostly the hotel wearing Jack's face, and the family's last hope narrows to the boy, his wounded mother, and the cook still battling to reach them.

Facing his possessed father, Danny refuses to flee and instead reminds the creature of the hotel's oldest duty: the basement boiler, which must be relieved of pressure every day or it will explode, and which Jack has forgotten. For an instant the true Jack surfaces, tells his son he loves him, and sends him away before the Overlook seizes him again and drives him to the boiler too late to save it. The pressure has passed the point of no return, and the hotel is destroyed in the blast, killing Jack and the malevolent presence together. Hallorann reaches the burning Overlook in time to carry Wendy and Danny out on the snowmobile. In a final summer scene the three are together at a resort in Maine where Hallorann now works; Wendy is recovering, and the cook comforts the grieving boy, telling him that his father truly loved him and that he must keep on living and feeling in spite of what the place did to them all.

characters.description: The narrator, a teenage girl who was turned into a vampire only a few months earlier and now lives among a large, violent group of newborn vampires in Seattle. Cautious, watchful, and eager simply to survive, she keeps to the edges of the chaotic pack, following the rules she is given without fully understanding what she has become or why. Behind her wariness she is thoughtful and quietly desperate for something like safety and friendship.
characters.name: Bree Tanner

characters.description: A newborn vampire who has lasted a little longer than most of the others and carries himself with unusual calm and self-control. Friendly and level-headed where the rest are feral and reckless, he takes an interest in Bree and becomes the closest thing she has to a friend, drawing her into questioning the strange life they have been forced into.
characters.name: Diego

characters.description: The handsome young vampire who commands the newborns, herding them indoors by day, organizing their nighttime hunts, and enforcing harsh rules with threats. He warns them of deadly dangers, including sunlight and a rival clan of enemies, and answers to an unseen master, a vampire the newborns almost never see. To Bree he is the frightening authority who controls their whole existence.
characters.name: Riley

characters.description: A large, standoffish newborn with an unusual gift: he radiates a repellent effect that makes others feel sick and instinctively look away from him, so the pack leaves him alone. Solitary and self-possessed, he keeps his distance from the violence, and Bree learns that staying near him offers a strange kind of protection.
characters.name: Fred

characters.description: The most brutal and dominant of the newborns, a swaggering bully who gathers a gang around him and delights in picking fights and destroying the weaker members of the pack. The others fear him, and Bree does her best to stay out of his path.
characters.name: Raoul

recaps.ending: Riley leads the newborn army into a forest near Forks to wipe out the rival clan they have been trained to hate, but the attack goes disastrously wrong and almost every newborn is destroyed. Bree, terrified, surrenders and is taken in by the enemy clan, a family of vampires who live without hunting humans and who treat her with surprising gentleness and even offer to protect her. Their kindness comes too late. The Volturi, the ancient rulers of the vampire world, arrive to make sure their secret laws have been kept and to clean up what remains of the illegal army. Although one of the family pleads for Bree's life and offers to take responsibility for her, the Volturi refuse. On the order of the merciless young Volturi guard Jane, Bree is executed. Her creator's scheme has collapsed, the friend she made is gone, and Bree, who wanted only to survive, dies knowing the truth of what was done to her and the others.
recaps.in_short: This companion novella follows Bree Tanner, a teenage girl recently turned into a vampire and living among a violent band of newborns in Seattle. Kept in the dark and controlled by a young vampire named Riley, the newborns are fed, hidden by day, and told lies, including that sunlight will destroy them. Bree befriends the calmer, older newborn Diego, and together they discover that the sunlight rule is false: it only makes their skin sparkle. They realize the whole army is being built and manipulated by a mysterious red-haired vampire, working through Riley, to attack a rival clan. Diego vanishes, and Bree, frightened, keeps her discovery secret and stays close to the solitary, self-protecting Fred. Riley marches the newborns to a forest near Forks to destroy their enemies, but the ambush fails and nearly all of them are killed. Bree surrenders to the enemy clan, who show her unexpected mercy, but the ancient vampire rulers, the Volturi, arrive to enforce their laws. Despite an offer to spare her, the Volturi order Bree's execution, and her short second life ends.

recaps.text: Bree Tanner is a teenage girl who was turned into a vampire only a few months ago and now lives among a large, unruly group of newborn vampires holed up in a house in Seattle. Created for a purpose none of them understands, the newborns are volatile and dangerous, forever fighting among themselves, and they are kept hidden indoors during the day and taken out at night to feed. A young vampire named Riley rules them, laying down strict rules and warning them of deadly threats, including sunlight and a clan of enemy vampires, while serving a master the newborns almost never see. Bree survives by staying quiet and out of the way, especially clear of the vicious bully Raoul. As the story opens she keeps her head down in this frightening new existence, beginning to sense that there is far more going on than Riley is telling any of them.

recaps.ending:
Haven's offensive fails at its decisive points. Parnell returns from the disastrous Yeltsin operation to find President Harris, the cabinet, and the leading legislaturalist families dead after the palace attack. The People's Quorum establishes a Committee of Public Safety under emergency powers, and the new authorities arrest Parnell for treason. Rollins has also been defeated after the Hancock operation.

At Hancock, Admiral Danislav's arrival closes the trap on Chin's pursuit, but the defense costs more than twelve thousand lives. HMS Nike is badly damaged, Admiral Sarnow survives with grave wounds, and his later recovery is unknown. Parks endorses Honor's decision to retain effective control when a formal transfer would have left the survivors without usable command information. He removes Pavel Young from command and recommends his court-martial for cowardice and desertion after Warlock abandons the formation. Honor departs for Manticore aboard Nike, carrying Young under arrest. Her fitness for command has been demonstrated, but Nike faces months of repair, her next assignment is unsettled, the future of her relationship with Tankersley is not recorded, and the wider war continues under Haven's new regime.
recaps.in_short: After recovering from grave injuries, Honor Harrington returns to command aboard HMS Nike and becomes Admiral Sarnow's flag captain at Hancock Station. The People's Republic engineers frontier attacks to disperse Manticore's forces, while Manticore answers with a false withdrawal from Yeltsin and a hidden reinforcement. Haven commits to attacks at Yeltsin and Hancock. Sarnow's weaker Hancock force uses missile pods, deception, and mines to delay Admiral Chin until Admiral Danislav arrives, but Nike is crippled and Sarnow is gravely wounded. Honor assumes effective control, saves Nike and Cassandra, and refuses to let Pavel Young's unauthorized flight break the remaining formation. Haven's expected quick victory instead becomes a series of defeats. A conspiracy destroys the presidential palace, kills President Harris and the old government, and creates a Committee of Public Safety. Admiral Parnell is arrested for treason, while Parks approves Honor's command decision and sends Nike home with Young under arrest for cowardice and desertion.

recaps.text: Previously: Honor Harrington served the Royal Manticoran Navy through the Basilisk crisis and a later operation at Grayson. Her service left her carrying responsibility for severe losses, including the death of Admiral Courvosier, and she suffered grave injuries that required extensive reconstruction and therapy. She now has a cybernetic left eye. Nimitz is Honor's bonded treecat and empathic companion.

So far this book: Honor completes her recovery and accepts command of the new battlecruiser HMS Nike. Her executive officer is Michelle Henke, an old academy friend who understands both Honor's survivor guilt and the hidden history behind her academy fight. Nike is assigned to Hancock Station as the intended flagship of Admiral Mark Sarnow's new battlecruiser squadron.

Hancock faces a growing Havenite presence at Seaford IX while also carrying responsibility for several vulnerable allies. The station leadership spreads some strength among those systems rather than concentrating it forward. Nike arrives with a fractured fusion-generator housing, leaving the ship at reduced power and requiring the repair base to open an armored compartment for a replacement. Captain Tankersley estimates fourteen weeks of work. Sarnow allows his existing flagship to leave as planned and decides to shift his staff aboard the immobilized Nike, giving Honor the immediate task of integrating a flag staff while her ship is repaired.

So far this book: Sarnow appoints Honor as his flag captain and tactical deputy, then begins turning an inexperienced collection of ships into a squadron. Early gunnery exercises expose serious coordination failures, but Sarnow treats them as shared problems and supports Honor's authority. Ernestine Corell helps organize the critiques. Tankersley explains his limited part in the Basilisk refit dispute, and Honor does not blame him. As Nike's repairs accelerate, he and Honor become regular sparring partners and begin dining together.

Beyond Hancock, the frontier crisis deepens. A freighter is destroyed before a Grayson cruiser can intervene, a concealed Havenite cruiser destroys a light attack craft at Zanzibar, and another force strikes sensors at Zuckerman before withdrawing. Manticore still lacks conclusive attribution for every incident, but the pattern appears coordinated. Thomas Caparelli initially favors quiet reinforcement. Hamish Alexander warns that the raids may be intended to scatter Manticore's strength and leave its important positions exposed. The Admiralty accepts that war may be approaching and prepares warnings for frontier commanders.

So far this book: Sarnow forces Admiral Parks to stop excluding Honor from task-force conferences, although Parks still distrusts her judgment. The frontier attacks are revealed as deliberate People's Republic policy. President Harris gives Admiral Parnell authority to trigger the final escalation, while Haven prepares diplomatic cover for the conflict. The operation becomes open war. Admiral Edward Pierre's four battlecruisers are destroyed at Talbot, but other attacks succeed, including the loss of a Manticoran cruiser.

Parks rejects Sarnow's proposal to concentrate near Seaford IX. He sends Hancock's wall-of-battle units to cover Yorick and Zanzibar, leaving Sarnow's lighter group to defend the station until Admiral Danislav can arrive. Sarnow and Honor prepare an asymmetric defense using upgraded missile pods, concealed communications, and fast minelayers, knowing they cannot win a prolonged engagement against capital ships. Elsewhere, Captain Helen Zilwicky commits five escorts against a stronger Havenite raiding force so her convoy can scatter. All five escorts are destroyed, but they inflict heavy losses and save the transports carrying her brother Anton and his daughter.

So far this book: Nike becomes the strongest gunnery ship in Sarnow's task group, and Honor demonstrates independent tactical command during an exercise. HMS Warlock then arrives under Captain Lord Pavel Young, the academy assailant who still blames Honor for his stalled career. Honor must receive him professionally despite his concealed desire for revenge. At the same time, Commander Ogilvy retrieves Operation Argus data showing that Hancock's main battle force has departed and prepares to carry the intelligence to Admiral Rollins.

Inside the People's Republic, Cordelia Ransom and selected political contacts join a conspiracy that intends to use a disastrous war as the opening for revolution. The group includes an Internal Security informant who secretly serves the plotters. Meanwhile, Manticore develops its own strategic deception. Thomas Caparelli proposes leaking a false order that makes Yeltsin appear weak while its defenders remain in place. Hamish Alexander supports the plan and proposes adding four Home Fleet squadrons under his command. Michael Mayhew formally accepts the danger to Grayson, and the government authorizes the trap.

So far this book: Parnell accepts Manticore's planted evidence that Yeltsin has been weakened and orders his available force to attack earlier than planned. He keeps the Seaford force separate. The revolutionary conspiracy also moves from planning to action: Cordelia Ransom prepares selected CRU cells, and a strike team assassinates the head of Internal Security.

At Seaford, Argus confirms that Hancock has lost its wall of battle. Admiral Chin warns that the intelligence may be a trap, but Admiral Rollins chooses to attack before reinforcements can arrive and sends Chin's faster squadron ahead. Near Yorick, Commander Tribeca detects a covert Havenite ship communicating with a concealed relay. Her discovery exposes the nature of the Argus surveillance network. Parks realizes that Sarnow's warning was correct and orders his dispersed forces to concentrate, but Hancock is already under threat. Sarnow detects roughly thirty-five Havenite capital ships with about seventy escorts while Danislav remains up to seventy-two hours away. He evacuates noncombatants, lays a minefield, and begins a low-signature maneuver intended to deliver a concealed opening strike.

So far this book: Sarnow's force ambushes Admiral Chin with pod-launched missiles and electronic warfare, destroying major ships before decoys draw the pursuers away from Hancock's repair base. Chin identifies the deception and continues after him, but a pre-laid minefield inflicts further losses. Manticoran ships are destroyed in the delaying action, including HMS Crusader, whose loss kills Commodore Van Slyke and leaves Pavel Young commanding the heavy cruisers.

Admiral Danislav arrives with dreadnoughts in time to cut off Chin, and Rollins turns away from the base. A missile strike cripples Nike, destroys its command center, and gravely wounds Sarnow. Honor retains effective control because the nominal senior captain lacks the information and communications needed to command. Young orders an unauthorized retreat and refuses Honor's order to return, but four of his cruisers rejoin her. Honor uses electronic warfare to cover the escape of Nike and Cassandra. Parks later approves her decision, arrests Young, and recommends a court-martial for cowardice and desertion.

The defeats at Hancock, Seaford, and Yeltsin accompany a coup in Haven. Assault shuttles destroy the presidential palace, killing President Harris and the old central government. A Committee of Public Safety takes power and arrests Parnell for treason. Nike begins the journey to Manticore for months of repairs with Young under arrest aboard her.

characters.description: A newly qualified Ranger facing the unfinished crisis at Castle Macindaw. Will has uncovered Keren's conspiracy but must now rescue Alyss and recover a powerful border fortress with only the allies he can gather locally.
characters.name: Will

characters.description: A Courier and Will's close friend, now held inside Macindaw after Keren's coup. She is trained to resist pressure and to notice political weaknesses, but Keren's blue gemstone gives him an unusual means of attacking that resistance.
characters.name: Alyss Mainwaring

characters.description: The usurper controlling Castle Macindaw. Keren poisoned Lord Syron and Orman, cultivated rumours of sorcery and took Alyss prisoner; he now intends to strengthen his position through an alliance with Scotti invaders.
characters.name: Keren

characters.description: Lord Syron's son and rightful acting master of Macindaw. Abrasive but innocent of the crimes blamed on him, Orman escaped Keren's coup only after being poisoned and remains desperately ill under Malcolm's care.
characters.name: Orman

characters.description: Orman's loyal secretary, physically timid but steadfast when his master is in danger. Xander escaped the castle with Will and helps establish Orman's lawful authority among their small group of allies.
characters.name: Xander

characters.description: A gifted healer who shelters outcasts in Grimsdell Wood. Malcolm's knowledge of medicines, performance and local superstition gives Will resources that can be turned against enemies who have made fear of sorcery part of their plan.
characters.name: Malcolm

characters.description: A scarred giant from Malcolm's community. Trobar is gentle with his friends but strong enough to shift obstacles that would stop ordinary men, making him valuable in any attempt to penetrate the castle.
characters.name: Trobar

characters.description: The dog Will rescued near Seacliff and later left with Alyss for protection. Shadow is fiercely attached to both of them and remains inside Macindaw with the prisoner.
characters.name: Shadow

characters.description: Will's closest friend and one of Araluen's finest young knights. Horace brings direct fighting strength to a problem Will cannot solve by stealth alone, while trusting Will to plan the campaign.
characters.name: Horace Altman

characters.description: Will's small Ranger horse, trained for silent movement and complex signals. Tug carries Will through his reconnaissance and links the Ranger to allies spread across the country around Macindaw.
characters.name: Tug

characters.description: A Skandian skirl whose failed raid on Seacliff ended in mutual respect between him and Will. Gundar commands a seasoned wolfship crew and believes he owes the young Ranger a debt.
characters.name: Gundar Hardstriker

characters.description: A Scotti operative held at Macindaw. His presence confirms that Keren's seizure of the castle is connected to a larger threat from across the northern border.
characters.name: MacHaddish

characters.description: The rightful lord of Macindaw, still incapacitated by the poison that began the conspiracy. Syron's survival matters because his authority can settle control of the fief once the castle is recovered.
characters.name: Lord Syron

recaps.ending: Will's improvised force takes Macindaw before the Scotti can turn it into the gateway for an invasion. Malcolm's staged effects and the reputation of Malkallam spread confusion, while Horace, Gundar's Skandians and Trobar provide the strength needed to penetrate and fight through the fortress. Alyss resists Keren's gemstone as the final struggle reaches her. Keren compels her to fire a crossbow at Will, but the mail he wears for the assault prevents the shot from killing him. Keren's control is broken and he is defeated. The Scotti plan collapses with the castle restored to its lawful side. Malcolm's treatment saves Orman and begins to restore Lord Syron, clearing away the false story that sorcery had destroyed the family. Will and Alyss are reunited, and their relief finally brings their feelings for each other into the open. Will completes his first major mission as a full Ranger with both the northern border and his friends safe, closing the continuous Macindaw story begun in The Sorcerer in the North.
recaps.in_short: Keren holds Castle Macindaw, Alyss and the northern gateway into Araluen, while Will has escaped with the poisoned Orman and Xander to Malcolm's refuge. With no army available in time, Will builds one from unlikely pieces: Horace, Malcolm's community and Gundar Hardstriker's Skandian crew. They combine reconnaissance, deception and Malcolm's theatrical version of sorcery with a physical assault through a hidden approach. Inside, Alyss struggles against Keren's blue gemstone, which he uses to extract information and weaken her will. Will's coalition enters the castle before Keren can deliver it to the Scotti. In the final confrontation Keren compels Alyss to shoot Will, but his mail prevents a fatal wound; her control is broken and Keren is defeated. Orman and Lord Syron recover under Malcolm's care, the invasion route is secured, and Will and Alyss acknowledge the love that their separation has made impossible to ignore.

recaps.text: Previously: Newly qualified as a Ranger, Will proved himself at Seacliff before being sent north in disguise to investigate reports of sorcery around Castle Macindaw. Lord Syron had fallen mysteriously ill, and suspicion centred on his unpopular son Orman. Will and the Courier Alyss discovered that the supposed sorcerer Malkallam was really Malcolm, a healer sheltering people driven from their homes by fear. Orman had been consulting him in secret to save Syron. The rumours were part of a conspiracy by Orman's popular cousin Keren, who poisoned the ruling family and intended to hand the border stronghold to Scotti invaders.
